newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SKODA FEBRUARY UNIT SALES UP 14 PCT - VW.
newsitem.headline: SKODA FEBRUARY UNIT SALES UP 14 PCT - VW.

text.p: Unit sales of Volkswagen AG Czech unit Skoda Automobilova a.s. rose 14 percent in February, an increase for the month above VW's own passenger cars and those of SEAT, but lower than Audi, a senior VW official said on Tuesday.
In an interview with Reuters at the Geneva car show, VW management board member Robert Buechelhofer said total group sales were up 13 percent to 660,000 in February, year-on-year.
Specific Skoda sales figures were not released.
Buechelhofer said that sales in the critical west European market were up about seven to eight percent for the month over the 1996 year-ago period.

But he said sales were down about four to six percent in Germany during February, in part due to the suspension of production for about a week of VW's Polo model due to parts shortages caused by the Spanish trucker's strike.
Buechelhofer however noted that incoming orders in Germany for the first two months of 1997 were up 30 percent and that he expected the sales situation to stabilise in the country.
"Incoming orders in Germany are going very well and have been above our expectations," he said. "The situation in Germany will work itself out."
He declined to provide forecasts for 1997 VW sales, saying "it would be speculative to talk about the full year".
But Buechelhofer noted that he expected VW to maintain the worldwide market share of about 10 percent, achieved in 1996, in 1997 despite weakening consumer demand for vehicles.
VW said provisional sales results for February showed eastern European sales rose 30 percent, while North American sales rose 27 percent.
In South America and Africa combined, the carmaker said sales were up 17 percent. Sales in the Asia-Pacific region rose 28 percent, including a 34 percent increase in sales in Japan.

Among VW's global brands, Buechelhofer said VW passenger car sales to customers during February rose 10 percent but fell four to six percent in Germany. But sales of trucks under the VW brand rose 30 percent, he said.
At VW's luxury car brand Audi, sales were up 28 percent while sales for Spanish-based SEAT were up eight percent.
